title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 52 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 398–402 (Night 52, continuing directly from nights-51), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 52 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Abrīza rebukes the slave al-Ghaḍbān in prose and verse and he answers in verse; when she insults his birth he kills her. Marjāna delivers the baby, and Abrīza's father, King Ḥardūb of the Rūm, arrives and learns what has happened. Back in Qaysāriyya his mother Dhāt al-Dawāhī persuades him to wait and to have learned Muslim sages train a group of girls to be sent against ʿUmar. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ وَالْخَمْسُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāniyatu wa-al-khamsūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the second-and-fifty,
sentences.i: And when it was the fifty-second night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ الْمَلِكَةَ أَبْرِيزَةَ لَمَّا قَالَتْ لِلْعَبْدِ الَّذِي هُوَ الْغَضْبَانُ مَا بَقِيَ عَلَيَّ إِلَّا الْعَبِيدُ السُّودَانُ بَعْدَ مَا كُنْتُ لَا أَرْضِي بِالْمُلُوكِ الصَّنَادِيدِ وَاغْتَاظَتْ مِنْهُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu-anna al-malikata Abrīzata lammā qālat li-al-ʿabdi alladhī huwa al-Ghaḍbānu mā baqiya ʿalayya illā al-ʿabīdu al-sūdānu baʿda mā kuntu lā arḍī bi-al-mulūki al-ṣanādīdi wa-ightāẓat minhu wa-qālat lahu
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king, the felicitous-one, that the queen Abrīza, when she said to the slave who is al-Ghaḍbān, "Nothing is left upon me but the black slaves, after I was not content with the champion kings," and she was enraged at him and said to him:
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when Queen Abrīza had said to the slave al-Ghaḍbān, "Nothing is left for me now but black slaves, after I would not be content even with champion kings," she flew into a rage against him and said to him:
sentences.n: The edition prints السَّعِيدُأَنَّ as a single word: the king's epithet السَّعِيدُ "the felicitous" run together with أَنَّ "that". We keep it as printed and vocalise both parts. The queen's "Nothing is left upon me but the black slaves" is what she had said at the end of the previous night; the narrator resumes from there. In ارضي the final yā' stands for the sound -ā (alif maqṣūra), as often in this print; we point it to match the spelling.

sentences.t: وَيْلَكَ مَا هَذَا الْكَلَامُ الَّذِي تَقُولُهُ لِي
sentences.tr: waylaka mā hādhā al-kalāmu alladhī taqūluhu lī
sentences.l: Woe-to-you! What is this speech which you say to me?
sentences.i: Curse you! What is this talk you address to me?
sentences.n: وَيْلَكَ is the stock exclamation of rebuke, literally "woe to you"; it recurs constantly in the Nights and does not need a literal "woe" every time.

sentences.t: وَيْلَكَ لَا تَتَفَوَّهْ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ هَذَا فِي حَضْرَتِي
sentences.tr: waylaka lā tatafawwah bi-shayʾin min hādhā fī ḥaḍratī
sentences.l: Woe-to-you! Do not open-your-mouth with a thing of this in my presence!
sentences.i: Curse you! Do not let a word of this pass your lips in my presence!

sentences.t: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّنِي لَا أَرْضَى بِشَيْءٍ مِمَّا قُلْتَهُ وَلَوْ سُقِيتُ كَأْسَ الرَّدَى
sentences.tr: wa-iʿlam annanī lā arḍā bi-shayʾin mimmā qultahu wa-law suqītu kaʾsa al-radā
sentences.l: And know that I am not content with a thing of what you have said, even if I were given-to-drink the cup of destruction.
sentences.i: Know that I will not agree to any of what you have said, even if I am made to drink the cup of death.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنِ اصْبِرْ حَتَّى أُصْلِحَ شَأْنَ الْجَنِينِ وَأُصْلِحَ شَأْنِي وَأَرْمَى الْخَلَاصَ ثُمَّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ إِنْ قَدَرْتَ عَلَيَّ اِفْعَلْ بِي مَا تُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: wa-lākini iṣbir ḥattā uṣliḥa shaʾna al-janīni wa-uṣliḥa shaʾnī wa-armā al-khalāṣa thumma baʿda dhālika in qadarta ʿalayya ifʿal bī mā turīdu
sentences.l: But be patient until I set-right the affair of the foetus and set-right my affair and aim-at the deliverance; then after that, if you are able over me, do to me what you want.
sentences.i: But be patient until I have put right the matter of the child in my womb, and put my own affairs in order, and made for my deliverance. After that, if you can master me, do with me what you will.
sentences.n: وَأرْمَى الْخَلَاصَ is obscure: رَمَى is "to throw, to aim", so the likeliest sense is "aim at, make for, deliverance". The print may hide a slip (perhaps أَرْجُوَ "hope for"). We vocalise it as printed. Note also that الْجَنِين is the unborn child, a reminder of the pregnancy that Abrīza has so far concealed from the slave.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ لَمْ تَتْرُكْ فَاحِشَ الْكَلَامِ فِي هَذَا الْوَقْتِ فَإِنِّي أَقْتُلُ نَفْسِي بِيَدِي وَأُفَارِقُ الدُّنْيَا وَأَرْتَاحُ مِنْ هَذَا كُلِّهِ وَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ
sentences.tr: wa-in lam tatruk fāḥisha al-kalāmi fī hādhā al-waqti fa-innī aqtulu nafsī bi-yadī wa-ufāriqu al-dunyā wa-artāḥu min hādhā kullihi wa-anshadat taqūlu
sentences.l: And if you do not leave off the foul-thing of speech at this time, then I will kill my soul with my hand, and take-leave-of the world, and be at-rest from all this; and she recited, saying:
sentences.i: And if you do not stop this foul talk now, I will kill myself with my own hand, take leave of the world, and be at rest from all of this. Then she recited, saying:

sentences.t:
اَيَا غَضْبَانُ دَعْنِي قَدْ كَفَانِيْ * مُكَابَدَةُ الْحَوَادِثِ وَالزَّمَانِ
عَنِ الْفَحْشَاءِ رَبِّي قَدْ نَهَانِيْ * وَقَالَ النَّارُ مَثْوَى مَنْ عَصَانِيْ
وَاِنِّي لَا اِمِيلُ لِفِعْلِ سُوءِ * بِعَيْنِ النَّقْصِ دَعْنِي لَاتَرَانِيْ
وَلَوْ لَمْ تَتْرُكِ الْفَحْشَاءَ عَنِّيْ * وَتَرْعَى حُرْمَتِي فِي مَنْ رَعَانِيْ
لَاصْرُخْ طَاقَتِيْ لِرِجَالِ قَوْمِيْ * وَاَجْلِبُ كُلَّ قَاصِيهَا وَدَانِيْ
وَلَوْ قَطَّعْتُ بِالسَّيْفِ الْيَمَانِيْ * لَمَا خَلَّيْتُ فَحَّاشًا يَرَانِيْ
مِنَ الْاَحْرَارِ وَالْكُبَرَاءِ طُرًّا * فَكَيْفَ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ نَسْلِ الزَّوَانِيْ
sentences.tr:
ayā Ghaḍbānu daʿnī qad kafānī * mukābadatu al-ḥawādithi wa-al-zamāni
ʿani al-faḥshāʾi rabbī qad nahānī * wa-qāla al-nāru mathwā man ʿaṣānī
wa-innī lā amīlu li-fiʿli sūʾin * biʿayni al-naqṣi daʿnī lā tarānī
wa-law lam tatruki al-faḥshāʾa ʿannī * wa-tarʿā ḥurmatī fī man raʿānī
la-aṣrukh ṭāqatī li-rijāli qawmī * wa-ajlibu kulla qāṣīhā wa-dānī
wa-law qaṭṭaʿtu bi-al-sayfi al-yamānī * lamā khallaytu faḥḥāshan yarānī
mina al-aḥrāri wa-al-kubarāʾi ṭurran * fa-kayfa al-ʿabdu min naslin al-zawānī
sentences.l:
O Ghaḍbān, leave me; enough for me * is the enduring of the misfortunes and of time.
From indecency my Lord has forbidden me * and said: The Fire is the lodging of him who disobeys me.
And I incline not to a deed of evil; * with the eye of deficiency, leave me, do not see me.
And if you do not leave indecency from me * and heed my sanctity regarding him who tended me,
I will cry out, with all my strength, to the men of my people * and summon every far-one of it and near-one;
And if I cut with the Yemeni sword * I would not let a lewd-one see me
of the free-born and the great-ones, all together; * so how a slave from the stock of the whores!
sentences.i:
O Ghaḍbān, let me be; I have had enough * of enduring the blows of fortune and of time.
My Lord has forbidden me all indecency * and has said that the Fire is the home of those who disobey him.
I will never lean toward an act of evil; * leave me, and do not look on me with the eye of contempt.
If you will not keep this filth away from me * and respect my honour toward the one who has sheltered me,
I will cry out with all my strength to the men of my people * and summon every one of them, far and near;
Even if I had to cut my way with the Yemeni sword * I would not leave a lecher alive who had seen me,
not among the freeborn and the noble, one and all. * How then a slave, from the stock of whores?
sentences.n: The print points these lines, and we copy them as printed. Several forms are loose: لَاصْرُخْ is la- (oath or purpose) + aṣrukh with a jussive ending, and تَرْعَى is indicative where the grammar after لَمْ would want a jussive. لَاتَرَانِيْ is printed as one word, lā tarānī, "do not see me". In the sixth line قَطَّعْتُ is pointed as an active "I cut"; the sense wanted is probably "even if I were cut to pieces", but we keep the print. The last half-line is a curse on his birth, echoed by Abrīza in her last speech below.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْغَضْبَانُ ذَلِكَ الشِّعْرَ غَضِبَ غَضَبًا شَدِيدًا وَاحْمَرَّتْ عَيْنَاهُ وَاغْبَرَّتْ سَجْنَتُهُ وَانْتَفَخَتْ مَنَاخِرُهُ وَاسْتَدَلَّتْ مَشَافِرُهُ وَزَادَتْ بِهِ النَّفَرَاتُ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-Ghaḍbānu dhālika al-shiʿra ghaḍiba ghaḍaban shadīdan wa-aḥmarrat ʿaynāhu wa-ighbarrat sajnatuhu wa-intafakhat manākhiruhu wa-istadallat mashāfiruhu wa-zādat bihi al-nafarātu wa-anshada yaqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And when al-Ghaḍbān heard that poetry, he was angry with a violent anger, and his two eyes reddened, and his complexion dusted-over, and his nostrils swelled, and his lips drooped, and the starts-of-fury increased in him, and he recited, saying these verses.
sentences.i: When al-Ghaḍbān heard her verses he was seized by a violent rage: his eyes reddened, his face went dark with dust, his nostrils swelled and his lips hung slack, and his fits of fury grew upon him. He recited these lines:
sentences.n: Several of these words are rare. سَجْنَتُهُ is "his face, his complexion" (Lane gives سَجْنَة); اغْبَرَّتْ, "turned dust-coloured", is the stock picture of a face darkened with fury. مَنَاخِر are nostrils and مَشَافِر the thick lips of a camel, used here in contempt. اسْتَدَلَّتْ is obscure and may be a slip (for example for اسْتَرْخَتْ "went slack"); we point it as printed and translate by the sense. نَفَرَات are starts or fits of shying, here of rage.

sentences.t:
اَيَا اَبْرِيزَةُ لَا تَتْرُكِينِيْ * قَتِيلَ هَوَاكِ بِاللَّحْظِ الْيَمَانِيْ
فَقَلْبِيْ قَدْ تَقَطَّعَ مِنْ جَفَاكِ * وَجِسْمِيْ نَاحِلٌ وَالصَّبْرُ فَانِ
وَطَرْفُكِ قَدْ سَبَى الْاَلْبَابَ سِحْرًا * وَعَقْلِيْ نَازِحٌ وَالشَّوْقُ دَانِ
وَلَوْ اَجْلَبْتِ مِلْأَ الْاَرْضِ جَيْشًا * لَا بْلُغَ مَا رَبِيْ فِيْ ذَا الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr:
ayā Abrīzatu lā tatrukīnī * qatīla hawāki bi-al-laḥẓi al-yamānī
fa-qalbī qad taqaṭṭaʿa min jafāki * wa-jismī nāḥilun wa-al-ṣabru fānī
wa-ṭarfuki qad sabā al-albāba siḥran * wa-ʿaqlī nāziḥun wa-al-shawqu dānī
wa-law ajlabti milʾa al-arḍi jayshan * la-ablugha mā rabī fī dhā al-zamāni
sentences.l:
O Abrīza, do not leave me * a man slain of your passion by the Yemeni glance;
For my heart is cut to pieces by your cruelty, * and my body is wasted, and patience is perishing.
And your eye has captivated the minds by sorcery, * and my reason is far-off, and longing is near.
And if you summoned an earth-full of army, * I would reach what my lord ... in this time.
sentences.i:
O Abrīza, do not leave me * slain by your love, by your Yemeni glance.
My heart is cut to pieces by your cruelty, * my body is wasted and my patience is spent.
Your eyes have taken minds captive by sorcery; * my reason has wandered far, and longing is close at hand.
Even if you called up an army to fill the earth, * I would still reach my aim in this time.
sentences.n: Again the print points the verse and we copy it. In the last line لَا بْلُغَ is the oath-particle la- with أَبْلُغَ split across two words, and مَا رَبِيْ is most likely مَأْرَبِي, "my aim, my desire", printed as two words: taken as printed it would be "what my lord", which makes no sense. The literal layer shows the printed words; the idiomatic layer gives the sense.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ أَبْرِيزَةُ كَلَامَهُ بَكَتْ بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا وَقَالَتْ لَهُ وَيْلَكَ يَاغَضْبَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat Abrīzatu kalāmahu bakat bukāʾan shadīdan wa-qālat lahu waylaka yā-Ghaḍbānu
sentences.l: And when Abrīza heard his speech, she wept a weeping, a violent one, and said to him: Woe-to-you, O Ghaḍbān!
sentences.i: When Abrīza heard what he said, she wept bitterly, and said to him: Curse you, Ghaḍbān!
sentences.n: The print writes يَاغَضْبَانُ as one word, يَا "O" run into the name; the name takes the nominative -u as a vocative addressed to a single person.

sentences.t: وَهَلْ بَلَغَ مِنْ قَدْرِكَ أَنْ تُخَاطِبَنِي بِهَذَا الْخِطَابِ يَا وَلَدَ الزِّنَا وَتَرْبِيَةَ الْخَنَى
sentences.tr: wa-hal balagha min qadrika an tukhāṭibanī bi-hādhā al-khiṭābi yā walada al-zinā wa-tarbiyata al-khanā
sentences.l: And has it reached, from your rank, that you address me with this address, O child of fornication, and rearing of lewdness?
sentences.i: Has your rank risen so high that you dare to address me in such words, you bastard, you brought up on filth?

sentences.t: أَتَحْسَبُ أَنَّ النَّاسَ كُلَّهُمْ سَوَاءٌ
sentences.tr: a-taḥsabu anna al-nāsa kullahum sawāʾun
sentences.l: Do you reckon that the people, all of them, are alike?
sentences.i: Do you suppose that all people are the same?

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْعَبْدُ النَّحْسُ ذَلِكَ مِنْهَا غَضِبَ وَاحْمَرَّتْ عَيْنَاهُ وَتَقَدَّمَ إِلَيْهَا وَضَرَبَهَا بِالسَّيْفِ فِي وَرَائِدِهَا فَقَتَلَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-ʿabdu al-naḥsu dhālika minhā ghaḍiba wa-aḥmarrat ʿaynāhu wa-taqaddama ilayhā wa-ḍarabahā bi-al-sayfi fī warāʾidihā fa-qatalahā
sentences.l: And when the slave, the ill-omened, heard that from her, he was angry, and his two eyes reddened, and he stepped forward to her and struck her with the sword in her ... and killed her.
sentences.i: When the accursed slave heard this from her, he flew into a rage, his eyes reddened, he stepped up to her, struck her with the sword across the neck, and killed her.
sentences.n: ورائدها is not a form we can place with confidence. The sense required is a vital part of her body, and the nearest candidate is وَرِيدِهَا, "her jugular vein" (or وَرَائِهَا, "from behind her"). We point the letters as printed, as it stands, and translate by the sense.

sentences.t: وَسَاقَ جَوَادَهَا بَعْدَ أَنْ أَخَذَ مِنَ الْمَالِ وَنَجَا بِنَفْسِهِ فِى الْجِبَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-sāqa jawādahā baʿda an akhadha mina al-māli wa-najā bi-nafsihi fī al-jibāli
sentences.l: And he drove off her horse, after he had taken from the money, and escaped with himself into the mountains.
sentences.i: He drove off her horse, after taking part of the money, and fled for his life into the mountains.
sentences.n: نَجَا بِنَفْسِهِ is the stock phrase "escaped with his own self", that is, barely with his life; the print spells فِى with the yā' for فِي.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْغَضْبَانِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā-kāna min amri al-Ghaḍbāni
sentences.l: This: what-was of the affair of al-Ghaḍbān.
sentences.i: So much for what became of al-Ghaḍbān.
sentences.n: مَاكَانَ is printed as one word, mā kāna ("what was"); we point it as the edition spells it. هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ … is the storyteller's stock way of closing one strand ("that is what happened with …") before turning to the next.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ فَإِنَّهَا وَلَدَتْ وَلَدًا ذَكَرًا مِثْلَ الْقَمَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-malikati Abrīzata fa-innahā waladat waladan dhakaran mithla al-qamari
sentences.l: And as for what was of the affair of the queen Abrīza, then indeed she bore a boy, a male, like the moon.
sentences.i: As for Queen Abrīza, she gave birth to a baby boy, bright as the moon.
sentences.n: وَأَمَّا … فَـ is the storyteller's switch of scene: "as for X, then …". The fa- after the long topic is a resumption marker, and إِنَّهَا is not emphatic here. ذَكَرًا ("a male") is stated outright, as the tale stresses that the child is a son.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْهُ مَرْجَانَةُ وَأَصْلَحَتْ شَأْنَهُ وَجَعَلَتْهُ إِلَى جَنْبِ أُمِّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhathu Marjānatu wa-aṣlaḥat shaʾnahu wa-jaʿalathu ilā janbi ummihi
sentences.l: And Marjāna took him, and set-right his condition, and made him to the side of his mother.
sentences.i: Marjāna took him up, tended to him, and laid him beside his mother.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ ثَدْيَهَا وَهِيَ مَيِّتَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha thadyahā wa-hiya mayyitatun
sentences.l: And he took her breast, and she a dead one.
sentences.i: and the baby took hold of her breast, though she was dead.
sentences.n: The subject of فَأَخَذَ is the newborn, who has just been laid beside his mother; the mother is already dead, struck down by Ghaḍbān's sword. وَهِيَ مَيِّتَةٌ is a circumstantial clause: "while she was dead". The grim detail is in the text and we keep it.

sentences.t: وَصَرَخَتْ صَرْخَةً عَظِيمَةً وَشَقَّتْ أَثْوَابَهَا وَحَثَتِ التُّرَابَ عَلَى رَأْسِهَا وَلَطَمَتْ عَلَى خَدَّيْهَا حَتَّى خَرَجَ الدَّمُ مِنْ وَجْهِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ṣarakhat ṣarkhatan ʿaẓīmatan wa-shaqqat athwābahā wa-ḥathati al-turāba ʿalā raʾsihā wa-laṭamat ʿalā khaddayhā ḥattā kharaja al-damu min wajhihā
sentences.l: And she screamed a scream, a great one, and split her garments, and cast the dust upon her head, and struck upon her two cheeks until the blood went out from her face.
sentences.i: And she screamed a great scream, tore her clothes, flung dust on her head and beat her cheeks until the blood ran from her face.
sentences.n: The subject is Marjāna, not the baby. Tearing the clothes, throwing dust on the head and beating the cheeks are the stock gestures of mourning. صَرَخَ صَرْخَةً is a cognate accusative ("screamed a scream"). The edition prints رَأْسِهَا with a precomposed hamza and we keep it.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ وَاسِتَاهْ وَاخَيْبَتَاهْ قُتِلْتِ مِنْ يَدِ عَبْدًا سُودٍ لَاقِيمَةَ لَهُ بَعْدَ فَرٍّ وَسِيتِكِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat wāsitāh wākhaybatāh qutilti min yadi ʿabdan sūdin lā-qīmata lahu baʿda farrin wa-sītiki
sentences.l: And she said: O-sitāh! O-the-disappointment-of-it! You were killed from the hand of a slave, black, no value to him, after a flight and your sīt.
sentences.i: And she said: "Alas, my shame! Alas, my ruin! You have been killed at the hand of a worthless black slave, after your flight and all your renown!"
sentences.n: This line is rough and partly obscure, and the print itself is uncertain. وَاسِتَاهْ is an exclamation of grief; it may be a clipped form of وَا سَوْأَتَاهْ ("alas, my shame"), and we read it so. وَاخَيْبَتَاهْ is wā + khaybat ("disappointment, ruin") + the long-ā + hā of lament. قُتِلْتِ is the passive "you were killed", addressed to the dead queen; the print marks the final kasra. عَبْدًا سُودٍ keeps the print's accusative-looking عَبْدًا after مِنْ يَدِ, which is Middle Arabic, and سُود is the plural "blacks" used as an adjective. لَاقِيمَةَ is لَا قِيمَةَ run together. Last, وَسِيتِكِ (the print marks the kasra on the kāf) is doubtful: we read it as ṣīt, "fame, renown" (written with sīn), but it could instead be a form of "your lady".

sentences.t: وَلَمْ تَزَلْ تَبْكِي
sentences.tr: wa-lam tazal tabkī
sentences.l: And she did not cease weeping.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِغُبَارٍ قَدْ طَلَعَ وَسَدَّ الْأَقْطَارَ فَانْكَشَفَ ذَلِكَ الْغُبَارُ وَبَانَ مِنْ تَحْتِهِ عَسْكَرٌ جَرَّارٌ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-ghubārin qad ṭalaʿa wa-sadda al-aqṭāra fa-inkashafa dhālika al-ghubāru wa-bāna min taḥtihi ʿaskarun jarrārun
sentences.l: And behold, with a dust that had risen and blocked the regions; then that dust uncovered itself, and there appeared from beneath it an army, a dragging one.
sentences.i: Suddenly a cloud of dust rose and blocked out the whole horizon; then the dust lifted, and from beneath it there appeared a vast army.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِـ is the "behold" of sudden appearance: the بِـ marks only what appears, and the dust is the thing that appears. عَسْكَرٌ جَرَّارٌ is a stock phrase for an immense host ("dragging", as it draws everything along behind it).

sentences.t: وَكَانَ هَذَا الْعَسْكَرُ عَسْكَرَ الْمَلِكِ حَرْدُوبَ وَالِدِ الْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna hādhā al-ʿaskaru ʿaskara al-maliki Ḥardūba wālidi al-malikati Abrīzata
sentences.l: And this army was the army of the king Ḥardūb, father of the queen Abrīza.

sentences.t: وَسَبَبُ ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ لَمَّا سَمِعَ أَنَّ ابْنَتَهُ هَرَبَتْ هِىَ وَجَوَارِبَهَا مِنْ بَغْدَادَ وَهِيَ عِنْدَ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ خَرَجَ بِمَنْ مَعَهُ يَتَشَمَّمُ الْأَخْبَارَ مِنْ بَعْضِ الْمُسَافِرِينَ إِنْ كَانُوا رَأَوْهَا عِنْدَ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-sababu dhālika annahu lammā samiʿa anna ibnatahu harabat hiya wa-jawāribahā min Baghdāda wa-hiya ʿinda al-maliki ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni kharaja bi-man maʿahu yatashammamu al-akhbāra min baʿḍi al-musāfirīna in kānū raʾawhā ʿinda al-maliki ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni
sentences.l: And the cause of that was that when he heard that his daughter had fled, she and her jawārib, from Baghdad, and she with the king ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān, he went out with whoever was with him, sniffing-out the news from some of the travellers, whether they had seen her with the king ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.i: The reason was this. When he heard that his daughter had fled from Baghdad with her maids, and that she was with King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, he rode out with his men to catch the scent of news from any travellers, hoping they had seen her at the court of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.n: جَوَارِبَهَا is printed with a bāʾ where the sense wants a yāʾ: it is surely جَوَارِيهَا, "her girls (maids)", with a one-dot slip, and we point the letters as printed. وَهِيَ عِنْدَ … is a circumstantial clause ("she being with …"). يَتَشَمَّمُ الْأَخْبَارَ, "sniffs out the news", is a vivid verb for enquiring; the following إِنْ كَانُوا رَأَوْهَا is the indirect question "whether they had seen her". رَأَوْهَا keeps the print's precomposed hamza.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا خَرَجَ وَبَعُدَ عَنْ بَلْدَتِهِ مَسِيرَةَ يَوْمٍ وَاحِدٍ رَأَى ثَلٰثَ فُرْسَانٍ مِنْ بَعِيدٍ فَقَصَدَهُمْ لِيَسْأَ لَهُمْ مِنْ أَيْنَ أَتَوْا وَيَعْلَمَ خَبَرَ ابْنَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kharaja wa-baʿuda ʿan baldatihi masīrata yawmin wāḥidin raʾā thalātha fursānin min baʿīdin fa-qaṣadahum li-yasʾala lahum min ayna atawā wa-yaʿlama khabara ibnatihi
sentences.l: And when he went out and was far from his town a journey of one day, he saw three horsemen from afar, and made for them to ask them from where they had come, and to know the news of his daughter.
sentences.i: When he had ridden out and was a day's journey from his town, he saw three horsemen in the distance and made for them, to ask them where they had come from and to learn news of his daughter.
sentences.n: ثَلٰثَ is the print's defective spelling of ثَلَاثَ, "three", and we mark it with the dagger alif; the number takes the genitive plural. The edition prints ليسأ and its next word لهم separately, with the hamza on the alif, and we keep both as printed. لِيَسْأَ … وَيَعْلَمَ are subjunctives of purpose after لِـ ("in order to ask … and to know"). مَسِيرَةَ يَوْمٍ is an accusative of measure ("to the extent of a day's journey").

sentences.t: وَكَانَ رَأَى عَلَى بُعْدِ هَؤُلَاءِ الثَّلٰثَةِ ابْنَتَهُ وَجَارِيَتَهَا وَالْعَبْدَ الْغَضْبَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna raʾā ʿalā buʿdi hāʾulāʾi al-thalāthati ibnatahu wa-jāriyatahā wa-al-ʿabda al-Ghaḍbāna
sentences.l: And he had seen, at a distance, these three: his daughter, and her girl, and the slave al-Ghaḍbān.
sentences.i: Now, at that distance, he had in fact seen his own daughter, her maid and the slave al-Ghaḍbān in those three riders.
sentences.n: كَانَ رَأَى is the pluperfect ("he had seen"), and the narrator lets us in on what Ḥardūb cannot yet know: the three horsemen are the very people he seeks. الثَّلٰثَةِ again has the dagger alif for ثَلَاثَةِ.

sentences.t: فَقَصَدَهُمْ لِيَسْأَ لَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qaṣadahum li-yasʾala lahum
sentences.l: And he made for them to ask them.
sentences.i: So he made for them, to put his questions to them.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَصَدَهُمْ خَافَ الْعَبْدُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ فَقَتَلَهَا وَنَجَا بِنَفْسِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qaṣadahum khāfa al-ʿabdu ʿalā nafsihi fa-qatalahā wa-najā bi-nafsihi
sentences.l: And when he made for them, the slave feared for his self, and killed her, and escaped with his self.
sentences.i: As he bore down on them, the slave feared for his life, killed her, and made his escape.
sentences.n: قَتَلَهَا: the "her" is Abrīza; the slave kills her in panic to save himself. نَجَا بِنَفْسِهِ is "escaped with his own skin", بِـ meaning "with", and نَفْس ("self") does the work of a reflexive pronoun.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَقْبَلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ رَأَهَا أَبُوهَا أَنَّهَا قُتِلَتْ وَجَارِيَتُهَا تَبْكِي عَلَيْهَا فَرَمَى نَفْسَهُ مِنْ فَوْقِ جَوَادِهِ وَوَقَعَ فِى الْأَرْضِ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aqbalū ʿalayhim raʾāhā abūhā annahā qutilat wa-jāriyatuhā tabkī ʿalayhā fa-ramā nafsahu min fawqi jawādihi wa-waqaʿa fī al-arḍi maghshiyyan ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And when they came upon them, her father saw her, that she was killed, and her girl weeping over her; and he threw himself from above his steed, and fell on the earth, one fainted-upon.
sentences.i: When they reached them, her father saw that she had been killed and that her maid was weeping over her. He threw himself from his horse and fell to the ground in a swoon.
sentences.n: رَأَهَا أَبُوهَا أَنَّهَا قُتِلَتْ is loose Middle Arabic: "her father saw her, that she was killed", with رَأَهَا keeping the print's precomposed hamza. مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ ("one covered over") is the idiom for fainting.

sentences.t: فَتَرَجَّلَ كُلُّ مَنْ كَانَ مَعَهُ مِنَ الْفُرْسَانِ وَالْأُمَرَاءِ وَالْوُزَرَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-tarajjala kullu man kāna maʿahu mina al-fursāni wa-al-umarāʾi wa-al-wuzarāʾi
sentences.l: And there dismounted everyone who was with him, of the horsemen and the commanders and the viziers.
sentences.i: All who rode with him dismounted, horsemen, emirs and viziers alike.

sentences.t: وَفِى الْحَالِ ضَرَبُوا الْخِيَامَ فِى الْجِبَالِ وَنَصَبُواقُبَّةً وَمُدَوَّرَةً لِلْمَلِكِ حَرْدُوبَ
sentences.tr: wa-fī al-ḥāli ḍarabū al-khiyāma fī al-jibāli wa-naṣabū-qubbatan wa-mudawwaratan li-al-maliki Ḥardūba
sentences.l: And in the moment they struck the tents in the mountains, and set up a dome and a round-one for the king Ḥardūb.
sentences.i: At once they pitched tents in the hills and set up a domed pavilion, round in shape, for King Ḥardūb.
sentences.n: The edition prints وَنَصَبُوا and قُبَّةً run together as one word, and we point them as two words glued, with the alif left silent. وَمُدَوَّرَةً ("and a round one") probably describes the same dome-tent, a round pavilion, rather than a second item. ضَرَبَ الْخِيَامَ, "struck the tents", is the usual verb for pitching them; the print has فِى with the dotless final form.

sentences.t: وَوَقَفَ أَرْبَابُ الدَّوْلَةِ بِظَاهِرِ تِلْكَ الْخَيْمَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-waqafa arbābu al-dawlati bi-ẓāhiri tilka al-khaymati
sentences.l: And the masters of the state stood at the outside of that tent.
sentences.i: The lords of the realm stood outside that tent.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْ مَرْجَانَةُ سَيِّدَهَا عَرَفَتْهُ وَزَادَتْ فِى الْبُكَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾat Marjānatu sayyidahā ʿarafathu wa-zādat fī al-bukāʾi
sentences.l: And when Marjāna saw her master, she knew him, and increased in the weeping.
sentences.i: When Marjāna saw her lord, she recognised him and wept all the harder.
sentences.n: سَيِّدَهَا is "her master", that is, Ḥardūb, her mistress's father, whom she therefore serves as well. The edition prints رَأَتْ with a precomposed hamza.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَ الْمَلِكُ مِنْ غَشْيَتِهِ وَسَأَلَهَا عَنِ الْخَبَرِ فَأَخْبَرَتْهُ بِالْقِصَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afāqa al-maliku min ghashyatihi wa-saʾalahā ʿani al-khabari fa-akhbaratuhu bi-al-qiṣṣati
sentences.l: And when the king recovered from his fainting, and asked her about the news, she informed him with the story.
sentences.i: When the king came to himself after his swoon and asked her what had happened, she told him the whole story.
sentences.n: The main clause is the last one: فَأَخْبَرَتْهُ بِالْقِصَّةِ, with فَ opening the answer to فَلَمَّا. أَخْبَرَ بِـ takes the thing told with بِـ.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنَّ الَّذِى قَتَلَ ابْنَتَكَ عَبْدٌ أَسْوَدُ مِنْ عَبِيدِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu inna al-ladhī qatala ibnataka ʿabdun aswadu min ʿabīdi ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni
sentences.l: And she said to him: Indeed the one who killed your daughter is a slave, a black, of the slaves of ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.i: And she said to him: "The one who killed your daughter is a black slave, one of ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān's slaves."

sentences.t: وَأَخْبَرَتْهُ بِمَا فَعَلَهُ الْمَلِكُ عُمَرُ بْنُ النُّعْمَانِ بِابْنَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhbaratuhu bi-mā faʿalahu al-maliku ʿUmaru ibnu al-Nuʿmāni bi-ibnatihi
sentences.l: And she informed him of what the king ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān had done to his daughter.
sentences.i: And she told him what King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān had done to his daughter.
sentences.n: بِابْنَتِهِ: here بِـ means "to" or "with" in the sense of "done to", since فَعَلَ بِـ is the verb's own preposition for the person acted on.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ حَرْدُوبُ ذَلِكَ اسْوَدَّتِ الدُّنْيَا فِي وَجْهِهِ وَبَكَى بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku Ḥardūbu dhālika iswaddati al-dunyā fī wajhihi wa-bakā bukāʾan shadīdan
sentences.l: And when the king Ḥardūb heard that, the world grew black in his face, and he wept a weeping, a violent one.
sentences.i: When King Ḥardūb heard this, the world went dark before his eyes, and he wept bitterly.
sentences.n: اسْوَدَّتِ الدُّنْيَا فِي وَجْهِهِ, "the world turned black in his face", is an idiom for despair and fury, "everything went black for him".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِإِحْضَارِ مِحْنَةٍ وَحَمْلِ ابْنَتِهِ فِيهَا وَمَضَى إِلَى قَيْسَارِيَةَ وَأَدْخَلُوهَا الْقَصْرَ
sentences.tr: thumma amara bi-iḥḍāri miḥnatin wa-ḥamli ibnatihi fīhā wa-maḍā ilā Qaysāriyyata wa-adkhalūhā al-qaṣra
sentences.l: Then he commanded the bringing of a miḥna, and the carrying of his daughter in it, and went to Caesarea, and they brought her into the palace.
sentences.i: Then he ordered a litter to be brought and his daughter to be carried in it, and he rode to Caesarea, where they took her into the palace.
sentences.n: مِحْنَةٍ as printed would mean "trial, ordeal", which makes no sense here; the sense calls for مِحَفَّة, "litter" (a bier-like carrying frame), and the print has probably a slip of one letter. We point it as printed and translate as "litter". أَمَرَ بِـ is the verb's own preposition ("command something"). قَيْسَارِيَةَ is Caesarea, here the Rūm king's seat.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ حَرْدُوبَ دَخَلَ عَلَى أُمِّهِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي وَقَالَ لَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika Ḥardūba dakhala ʿalā ummihi Dhāti al-Dawāhī wa-qāla lahā
sentences.l: Then indeed the king Ḥardūb entered upon his mother, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, and said to her:
sentences.i: Then King Ḥardūb went in to his mother, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, and said to her:
sentences.n: ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي is the old queen's by-name, "she of the calamities", for her cunning.

sentences.t: أَهَكَذَا تَفْعَلُ الْمُسْلِمُونَ بِبِنْتِي
sentences.tr: a-hakadhā tafʿalu al-muslimūna bi-bintī
sentences.l: Is it thus that the Muslims do to my daughter?
sentences.i: "Is this how the Muslims treat my daughter?"
sentences.n: تَفْعَلُ is feminine singular though الْمُسْلِمُونَ is a masculine plural; the print agrees the verb loosely, which is common in speech and we point as printed.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ الْمَلِكَ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ يَأُخُذُ وَجْهَهَا قَهْرًا وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ يَقْتُلُهَا عَبْدٌ أَسْوَدُ مِنْ عَبِيدِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-inna al-malika ʿUmara ibna al-Nuʿmāni yaʾkhudhu wajhahā qahran wa-baʿda dhālika yaqtuluhā ʿabdun aswadu min ʿabīdihi
sentences.l: For indeed the king ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān takes her face by force, and after that a slave, a black, of his slaves kills her.
sentences.i: "King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān takes her by force, and after that a black slave of his kills her!"
sentences.n: The print has a damma on the alif in يَأُخُذُ, and we keep it where the edition puts it; the word is the ordinary يَأْخُذُ, "he takes". أَخَذَ وَجْهَهَا is hard to render closely: "takes her face" is the sort of phrase that means having one's way with her, and in context it says that ʿUmar took her by force. We keep the plain sense and do not soften it.

sentences.t: فَوَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ لَابُدَّ مِنْ أَخْذِنَا ثَأُرَ بِنْتِي مِنْهُ وَكَشْفِ الْعَارِ عَنْ عِرْضِي وَإِلَّاقَتَلْتُ نَفْسِي بِيَدِي
sentences.tr: fa-wa-ḥaqqi al-Masīḥi lā-budda min akhdhinā thaʾra bintī minhu wa-kashfi al-ʿāri ʿan ʿirḍī wa-illā-qataltu nafsī bi-yadī
sentences.l: So by the right of the Messiah, there is no avoiding our taking the vengeance of my daughter from him, and the uncovering of the shame from my honour; and if not, I will kill myself by my hand.
sentences.i: "By the Messiah's truth, we must take vengeance on him for my daughter and wipe the shame from my honour, or else I will kill myself with my own hand!"
sentences.n: فَوَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ is an oath: the وَ is the oath-particle ("by the right of the Messiah"), with فَ before it linking to what was said. لَابُدَّ مِنْ is "there is no escaping", with لَا and بُدَّ run together as printed. The print has a damma on the alif in ثَأُرَ, and we keep it where it stands; the word is ثَأْرَ, "blood-vengeance". وَإِلَّا is the printed run-together of وَ + إِلَّا: "and if not".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَكَى بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: thumma bakā bukāʾan shadīdan
sentences.l: Then he wept a weeping, a violent one.
sentences.i: Then he wept bitterly.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ أُمُّهُ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي مَاقَتَلَ ابْنَتَكَ إِلَّامَرْجَانَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu ummuhu Dhātu al-Dawāhī mā-qatala ibnataka illā-Marjānatu
sentences.l: And she said to him, his mother Dhāt al-Dawāhī: Killed not your daughter except Marjāna.
sentences.i: Then his mother, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, said to him: No one killed your daughter but Marjāna.
sentences.n: The print runs two pairs of words together: مَاقَتَلَ is مَا قَتَلَ ("none killed"), and إِلَّامَرْجَانَةُ is إِلَّا مَرْجَانَةُ ("except Marjāna"). We keep the printed word divisions. Dhāt al-Dawāhī means "she of the calamities", the old queen's nickname.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّهَا كَانَتْ تَكْرَهُهَا فِى الْبَاطِنِ
sentences.tr: li-annahā kānat takrahuhā fī al-bāṭini
sentences.l: Because she was hating her in the inward.
sentences.i: For she secretly hated her.
sentences.n: فِى is printed with a final alif maqṣūra-style yā (ى) rather than the usual ي; we point the printed letters. فِي الْبَاطِنِ, "in the inward", means "in secret, at heart".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لِوَلَدِهَا لَاتَحْزَنْ مِنْ جِهَةِ أَخْذِ ثَأْرِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma qālat li-waladihā lā-taḥzan min jihati akhdhi thaʾrihā
sentences.l: Then she said to her son: Do not grieve from the side of taking her blood-vengeance.
sentences.i: Then she said to her son: Do not grieve over the matter of taking vengeance for her.

sentences.t: فَوَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ لَا أَرْجِعُ عَنِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ حَتَّى أَقْتُلَهُ وَأَقْتُلَ أَوْلَادَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-wa-ḥaqqi al-Masīḥi lā arjiʿu ʿani al-maliki ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni ḥattā aqtulahu wa-aqtula awlādahu
sentences.l: And by the right of the Messiah, I will not turn back from the king ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān until I kill him and kill his children.
sentences.i: By the Messiah's truth, I will not turn back from King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān until I have killed him and killed his sons.
sentences.n: وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ is an oath formula, "by the right (truth) of the Messiah"; الْمَسِيحُ is Christ, as befits a queen of the Rūm.

sentences.t: وَلَأَ عْمَلَنَّ مَعَهُ عَمَلًا تَعْجِزُ عَنْهُ الدُّهَاةُ وَالْأَبْطَالُ وَيَتَحَدَّثُ بِهِ الْمُحَدِّثُونَ فِي جَمِيعِ الْأَقْطَارِ وَفِي كُلِّ مَكَانٍ
sentences.tr: wa-laʾa ʿmalanna maʿahu ʿamalan taʿjizu ʿanhu al-duhātu wa-al-abṭālu wa-yatahaddathu bihi al-muḥaddithūna fī jamīʿi al-aqṭāri wa-fī kulli makānin
sentences.l: And I will surely do with him a deed that the crafty and the heroes are unable to match, and the tellers will tell of it in all the regions and in every place.
sentences.i: And I will do to him a deed that the cunning and the heroes would be powerless to do, and that the storytellers will tell of in every land and every place.
sentences.n: The print divides وَلَأَعْمَلَنَّ ("and I will surely do") after its second letter, as وَلَا عملن. We keep the printed division, so the verb's opening hamza falls at the end of the first word. تَعْجِزُ عَنْهُ means "is unable to (match) it".

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ يَنْبَغِي لَكَ أَنْ تَمْتَثِلَ أَمْرِي فِي كُلِّ مَا أَقُولُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin yanbaghī laka an tamtathila amrī fī kulli mā aqūluhu
sentences.l: But it is fitting for you that you comply with my command in everything that I say.
sentences.i: But you must follow my instructions in all that I tell you.

sentences.t: فَمَنْ نَوَى عَلَى مَا يُرِيدُ يَبْلُغْ مَا يُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: fa-man nawā ʿalā mā yurīdu yablugh mā yurīdu
sentences.l: For whoever intends upon what he wants will reach what he wants.
sentences.i: For whoever is set upon what he wants will reach what he wants.
sentences.n: A maxim in form. The jussive يَبْلُغْ is the answer to the conditional مَنْ; the sentence is pointed as a rule, with the second يُرِيدُ resumed. نَوَى عَلَى is "resolve upon".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ لَا أُخَالِفُكِ أَبَدًا فِيمَا تَقُولِينَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā wa-ḥaqqi al-Masīḥi lā ukhālifuki abadan fīmā taqūlīnahu
sentences.l: So he said to her: And by the right of the Messiah, I will not oppose you ever in what you say.
sentences.i: So he said to her: By the Messiah's truth, I will never go against you in anything you say.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ لَهُ اِئْتِنِي بِجَوَارٍ نُهَّدٍ أَبْكَارٍ وَائْتِنِي بِحُكَمَاءِ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: qālat lahu iʾtinī bi-jawārin nuhhadin abkārin wa-iʾtinī bi-ḥukamāʾi al-zamāni
sentences.l: She said to him: Bring me girls, high-breasted, virgins, and bring me the sages of the age,
sentences.i: She said to him: Bring me young girls, full-breasted virgins, and bring me the wise men of the age,
sentences.n: جَوَارٍ is the plural of جَارِيَة, "girl, slave-girl". نُهَّد (plural of نَاهِد) means girls whose breasts are just swelling; أَبْكَار are virgins. اِئْتِ بِـ is "bring" (the verb chooses the preposition).

sentences.t: وَدَعْهُمْ يُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ الْحِكْمَةَ وَالْأَدَبَ مَعَ الْمُلُوكِ وَالْمُنَادَمَةَ وَالْأَشْعَارَ
sentences.tr: wa-daʿhum yuʿallimūnahunna al-ḥikmata wa-al-adaba maʿa al-mulūki wa-al-munādamata wa-al-ashʿāra
sentences.l: and let them teach them wisdom and courtly manners with kings, and boon-companionship, and poems,
sentences.i: and have them teach the girls wisdom, the manners of kings' company, the art of the boon-companion, and poetry,
sentences.n: يُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ keeps its final -ūna where Classical grammar would drop it after دَعْهُمْ; we point what the text says. الْمُنَادَمَة is the art of being a king's drinking-companion.

sentences.t: وَيَتَكَلَّمُونَ مَعَهُنَّ بِالْحِكْمَةِ وَالْمَوَاعِظِ
sentences.tr: wa-yatakallamūna maʿahunna bi-al-ḥikmati wa-al-mawāʿiẓi
sentences.l: and let them speak with them with wisdom and with exhortations,
sentences.i: and let them converse with them in words of wisdom and counsel,

sentences.t: وَيَكُونُ الْحُكَمَاءُ مُسْلِمِينَ حَتَّى يُعَلِّمُوهُنَّ أَخْبَارَ الْعَرَبِ وَتَوَارِيخَ الْخُلَفَاءِ وَأَخْبَارَ مَنْ سَلَفَ مِنْ مُلُوكِ الْإِسْلَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-yakūnu al-ḥukamāʾu muslimīna ḥattā yuʿallimūhunna akhbāra al-ʿarabi wa-tawārīkha al-khulafāʾi wa-akhbāra man salafa min mulūki al-islāmi
sentences.l: and let the sages be Muslims, so that they teach them the reports of the Arabs and the histories of the caliphs and the reports of whoever has gone before of the kings of Islam.
sentences.i: and let the sages be Muslims, so that they may teach them the lore of the Arabs, the histories of the caliphs, and the stories of the Muslim kings of old.
sentences.n: The queen wants Muslim teachers so that the girls will know the culture of the court they are to enter. The two verbs يَتَكَلَّمُونَ and يَكُونُ continue the command in the indicative, in the manner of the text.

sentences.t: وَلَوْ أَقَمْنَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ أَرْبَعَةَ أَعْوَامٍ لَبَلَغْنَا الْمَرَامَ
sentences.tr: wa-law aqamnā ʿalā dhālika arbaʿata aʿwāmin la-balaghnā al-marāma
sentences.l: And if we stayed upon that four years, we would reach the aim.
sentences.i: And even if we spend four years on this, we will reach our goal.

sentences.t: فَطَوِّلْ رُوحَكَ وَاصْبِرْفَإِنَّ بَعْضَ الْأَعْرَابِ يَقُولُ إِنَّ أَخْذَ الثَّأْرِ بَعْدَ أَرْبَعِينَ عَامًا قَلِيلٌ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭawwil rūḥaka wa-iṣbir-fa-inna baʿḍa al-aʿrābi yaqūlu inna akhdha al-thaʾri baʿda arbaʿīna ʿāmin qalīlun
sentences.l: So lengthen your spirit, and be patient, for some of the Bedouin say: Taking vengeance after forty years is little.
sentences.i: So be patient and long-suffering, for one of the Bedouin says that vengeance taken after forty years is still soon.
sentences.n: طَوِّلْ رُوحَكَ, "lengthen your spirit", means "be patient". The print runs وَاصْبِرْ and فَإِنَّ together as one word, وَاصْبِرْفَإِنَّ, and we keep that. قَلِيلٌ, "little", is the old saying: even forty years is a short wait for vengeance.

sentences.t: وَنَحْنُ إِذَا عَلَّمْنَا تِلْكَ الْجَوَارِيَ بَلَغْنَا مِنْ عَدُوِّنَا مَا نَخْتَارُ
sentences.tr: wa-naḥnu idhā ʿallamnā tilka al-jawāriya balaghnā min ʿaduwwinā mā nakhtāru
sentences.l: And we, when we have taught those girls, will reach from our enemy what we choose,
sentences.i: And once we have taught those girls, we will have of our enemy whatever we choose,

sentences.t: لِأَنَّهُ مُمْتَحَنٌ بِحُبِّ الْجَوَارِي
sentences.tr: li-annahu mumtaḥanun bi-ḥubbi al-jawārī
sentences.l: because he is tried by the love of girls.
sentences.i: for he is plagued by a love of girls.
sentences.n: مُمْتَحَنٌ is "tried, put to the test", here afflicted by his passion for slave-girls. The preposition بِـ after it marks what he is tried by.

sentences.t: وَعِنْدَهُ ثَلٰثُمِائَةٍ وَسِتٌّ وَسِتُّونَ جَارِيَةً وَازْدَدْنَ مِائَةَ جَارِيَةٍ مِنْ خَوَاصِّ جَوَارِيكَ الَّتِي كُنَّ مَعَ الْمَرْحُومَةِ بِنْتِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿindahu thalāthumiʾatin wa-sittun wa-sittūna jāriyatan wa-izdadna miʾata jāriyatin min khawāṣṣi jawārīka allatī kunna maʿa al-marḥūmati bintika
sentences.l: And at him are three hundred and six and sixty girls, and they increased a hundred girls from the special ones of your girls who were with the mercied one, your daughter.
sentences.i: He has three hundred and sixty-six girls, and they have been increased by a hundred, chosen from your own girls who were with your late daughter.
sentences.n: ثَلٰثُمِائَةٍ is printed without its alif (ثلثمائة); we point it as ثَلَاثُمِائَةٍ with a dagger alif. وَازْدَدْنَ is uncertain: we read it as a past tense, "and they were increased", but it may be meant as a command, "and add (to them)". الْمَرْحُومَة, "the one granted mercy", is the way of saying "the late".

sentences.t: فَإِذَا تَعَلَّمَتِ الْجَوَارِي مَا قُلْتُ لَكَ عَلَيْهِ أَخَذْتُهُنَّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ وَأُسَافِرُ بِهِنَّ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā taʿallamati al-jawārī mā qultu laka ʿalayhi akhadhtuhunna baʿda dhālika wa-usāfiru bihinna
sentences.l: And when the girls have learned what I said to you upon it, I will take them after that, and I will travel with them.
sentences.i: When the girls have learned what I told you, I will take them after that and travel with them.
sentences.n: The verb أَخَذْتُهُنَّ is in the past tense but means "I will take them", the past of the condition. سَافَرَ بِـ is "travel with".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ حَرْدُوبُ كَلَامَ أُمِّهِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي فَرِحَ وَقَامَ وَقَبَّلَ رَأْسَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku Ḥardūbu kalāma ummihi Dhāti al-Dawāhī fariḥa wa-qāma wa-qabbala raʾsahā
sentences.l: And when the king Ḥardūb heard the speech of his mother Dhāt al-Dawāhī, he rejoiced and rose and kissed her head.
sentences.i: When King Ḥardūb heard what his mother Dhāt al-Dawāhī said, he was glad, and he rose and kissed her head.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَ مِنْ وَقْتِهِ وَسَاعَتِهِ الْمُسَافِرِينَ وَالْقُصَّادَ إِلَى أَطْرَٰفِ الْبِلَادِ لِيَأْتُوا إِلَيْهِ بِالْحُكَمَاءِ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: thumma arsala min waqtihi wa-sāʿatihi al-musāfirīna wa-al-quṣṣāda ilā aṭrāfi al-bilādi li-yaʾtū ilayhi bi-al-ḥukamāʾi mina al-muslimīna
sentences.l: Then he sent, from his time and his hour, the travellers and the messengers to the extremities of the lands, so that they bring to him the sages from the Muslims.
sentences.i: Then he sent out at once couriers and messengers to the farthest corners of the lands, to bring him sages from among the Muslims.
sentences.n: مِنْ وَقْتِهِ وَسَاعَتِهِ, "from his time and his hour", is a stock phrase for "that very moment". أَطْرَٰفِ is printed without its alif (اطرف); we point it as أَطْرَافِ with a dagger alif.

sentences.t: فَامْتَثَلُوا أَمْرَهُ وَسَافَرُوا إِلَى بِلَادٍ بَعِيدَةٍ وَأَتَوْهُ بِمَا طَلَبَهُ مِنَ الْحُكَمَاءِ وَالْعُلَمَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-imtathalū amrahu wa-sāfarū ilā bilādin baʿīdatin wa-atawhu bi-mā ṭalabahu mina al-ḥukamāʾi wa-al-ʿulamāʾi
sentences.l: So they complied with his command and travelled to distant lands, and they came to him with what he had asked for of sages and learned men.
sentences.i: They obeyed his command and travelled to far countries, and brought him the sages and scholars he had asked for.
sentences.n: أَتَى بِـ is "bring" (the verb chooses the preposition): أَتَوْهُ بِمَا, "they came to him with what".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ أَكْرَمَهُمْ غَايَةَ الْإِكْرَامِ وَخَلَعَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْخِلَعَ وَرَتَّبَ لَهُمُ الرَّوَاتِبَ وَالْجِرَايَاتِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ḥaḍarū bayna yadayhi akramahum ghāyata al-ikrāmi wa-khalaʿa ʿalayhimu al-khilaʿa wa-rattaba lahumu al-rawātiba wa-al-jirāyāti
sentences.l: And when they were present between his two hands, he honoured them the extreme of honouring, and bestowed upon them robes of honour, and ordained for them stipends and allowances,
sentences.i: When they stood before him he honoured them most highly, bestowed robes of honour upon them, and appointed for them salaries and rations,

sentences.t: وَوَعَدَهُمْ بِالْمَالِ الْجَزِيلِ إِذَا عَلَّمُوا الْجَوَارِيَ
sentences.tr: wa-waʿadahum bi-al-māli al-jazīli idhā ʿallamū al-jawāriya
sentences.l: and promised them abundant wealth if they taught the girls.
sentences.i: and promised them great wealth if they taught the girls.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَحْضَرَ لَهُمُ الْجَوَارِيَ
sentences.tr: thumma aḥḍara lahumu al-jawāriya
sentences.l: Then he had the girls brought before them.
sentences.i: Then he brought the girls before them.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُ—بَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mu—bāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving off the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The edition prints الْمُ—بَاحِ with a dash in the middle of the word; the word is the usual الْمُبَاحِ, "the permitted", of the closing formula, and we keep the dash as printed.
